metadata.rules_text:
- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially after recent spikes; apply downward bias correction by 5–15% for 30-day forecasts following price surges.
- Forecasting horizon 30d shows strong mean reversion bias — model fails to adjust downward after initial peaks; reduce forecasted values by 2–5% for each subsequent day after a peak.
- Sentiment history is uniformly neutral (0.00) across all examples — no sentiment-driven adjustment needed; model should not react to sentiment unless sentiment deviates from zero.
- Overshoot after spikes is common — model peaks too high and then falls sharply; apply a “cool-down” rule: reduce forecast by 10–20% from peak day onward for 3–5 days.
- Model exhibits persistent lag in recognizing downward trends — true prices drop faster than forecast; adjust for lag by adding 1–3 days of downward drift in forecast if recent history shows accelerating decline.
- No horizon-specific error observed — 30d forecasts are consistently overconfident; apply a “conservative smoothing” rule: average 3–5 prior days’ true values before forecasting next day to reduce volatility bias.
